column1: # Two metric layers: total util.gpu (legacy) and per-process sm% (new).
# Total util.gpu is dominated by the user's WM `sol` (steady ~11-25% sm)
# regardless of soltty load; per-process SM% via `nvidia-smi pmon -s u`
# is the only number that isolates soltty's actual contribution.
# Per-frame breakdown via SOLTTY_GPU_TIMING during cmatrix maximized:
# At ~120 fps the *draw* portion accounts for only ~3% util.gpu — the
# observed 25% lives in the swap/present pipeline (WM compositing).
# B. Per-process SM% (nvidia-smi pmon -s u) — the real signal
# 1. soltty's own SM% is noise floor (0-2% mean during cmatrix).
# 2. WM `sol` scales ~linearly with soltty's swap_buffers rate:
# 3. Damage tracking *inside* soltty won't help: each swap_buffers
#    signals "surface dirty" to the compositor regardless of which
#    cells changed. The big lever is fewer swaps, not less per-swap.
# 4. 30Hz seems to be a sweet spot: matches cmatrix native (~20Hz) and
#    drops WM to its idle baseline.
#   C2 first — drop default frame cap + tune burst throttle so the WM
#             sees ~30Hz of damage during cmatrix-like workloads.
#   C1 next — damage tracking still saves soltty CPU (prepare 310µs→
#   C3 skip — packing helps neither WM nor a 4090's GPU; defer.
# Alternating-runs A/B (3 each), cmatrix maximized, sol sm% mean:
#   prepare mean=384µs (was 311µs; per-frame work larger because fewer frames absorb more data)
# Per-frame is larger but per-second total is similar; WM compositor savings come from fewer swap_buffers calls.
